Our Purpose

At Deloitte, our Purpose is to make an impact that matters. We exist to inspire and help our people, organizations, communities, and countries to thrive by building a better future. Our work underpins a prosperous society where people can find meaning and opportunity. It builds consumer and business confidence, empowers organizations to find imaginative ways of deploying capital, enables fair, trusted, and functioning social and economic institutions, and allows our friends, families, and communities to enjoy the quality of life that comes with a sustainable future. And as the largest 100% Canadian-owned and operated professional services firm in our country, we are proud to work alongside our clients to make a positive impact for all Canadians.

By living our Purpose, we will make an impact that matters.

Have many careers in one Firm.
Enjoy flexible, proactive, and practical benefits that foster a culture of well-being and connectedness.
Learn from deep subject matter experts through mentoring and on the job coaching

Deloitte Global is the engine of the Deloitte network. Our professionals reach across disciplines and borders to develop and lead global initiatives. We deliver strategic programs and services that unite our organization.

What will your typical day look like?

Work you'll do

Deloitte Global is the engine of the Deloitte network. Our professionals reach across disciplines and borders to develop and lead global initiatives. We deliver strategic programs and services that unite our organization.

The Director, Data Management Capabilities & AI Readiness is responsible for defining and leading the strategy, operating model, and delivery of enterprise data management capabilities.

The role is the business owner for cross-domain data management capabilities that serve the Deloitte network, including Master Data Management (MDM), Metadata Management, Data Quality, Taxonomy Management, Reference Data, and Data Modeling.

Working across global applications, business functions, architecture teams, product organizations, and operational teams, the Director will establish scalable data management capabilities, drive adoption of enterprise standards and procedures, and develop trusted data assets for business operations, analytics, AI, regulatory compliance, and decision-making.

This leader serves as a key connector between business executives, application owners, enterprise architects, operations leaders, and technology teams, aligning diverse stakeholder perspectives and driving consensus on complex data management decisions across a global organization. This role is expected to establish measurable outcomes, monitor performance, and continuously evolve enterprise data management capabilities to an aligned target state and maturity model that the role will also define and govern.

The DSGO is responsible for building an integrated strategy and operating model to manage global data and AI products across their lifecycle, enabling better business outcomes, innovation, and client service.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Leadership
Define and execute the data management strategy for:
Master Data Management
Metadata Management
Ontology and Context Management
Data Quality
Taxonomy and Reference Data
Enterprise Data Models

Develop multi-year roadmaps that align to business priorities, digital transformation objectives, and AI enablement goals.
Establish and evolve enterprise operating models, governance forums, stewardship structures, and accountability frameworks.
Champion the importance of trusted, governed data as a strategic enterprise asset.
Lead a global team of data management professionals and subject matter experts.
Data Management Operating Model Development
Design and implement sustainable operating models supporting global and regional data domains.
Define roles, responsibilities, decision rights, escalation paths, and governance forums.
Build effective collaboration models between:
Business teams
Application owners
Product teams
Enterprise Architecture
Operations teams
Data and analytics functions

Establish service delivery models that enable consistent execution across multiple geographies and applications.
Drive adoption of standardized data management processes for, metadata, data quality, data architecture, taxonomy, and data quality remediation.
Master Data & Reference Data Management
Lead enterprise master data governance programs across key domains such as Customer, Vendor, Products, and People.
Define authoritative sources, golden record strategies, hierarchy management approaches, and lifecycle management approaches.
Establish data management practices for reference data and shared enterprise dimensions.
Partner with business and technology leaders to modernize master data capabilities and improve operational efficiency.
Metadata, Taxonomy & Data Modeling
Establish enterprise metadata management capabilities including technical, operational, and AI metadata.
Enable the integration of business glossaries and semantic frameworks across applications and data products.
Lead development of conceptual, logical, and physical data modeling standards.
Ensure enterprise data structures support interoperability, analytics, AI, and future platform modernization initiatives.
Data Quality & Measurement
Lead enterprise data quality management capabilities including strategy, frameworks, procedures, monitoring, and remediation
Operationalize quality dimensions, monitoring capabilities, issue management processes, and continuous improvement practices.
Partner with business and technology teams to improve the quality, consistency, integrity and usability of enterprise data across critical business domains.
Define and implement enterprise measurement frameworks, KPIs, and scorecards to assess the effectiveness and maturity of data management capabilities, including data issue resolution and remediation
Build executive dashboards and performance reporting that provide visibility into enterprise data health, operational performance, risks, and business outcomes.
Drive continuous improvement programs using quantitative performance measures, automation and operational metrics to increase the effectiveness of enterprise data management.
Stakeholder Management & Executive Influence
Build trusted relationships with senior executives, business leaders, product leaders, architects, and operations leaders.
Facilitate decision-making across highly complex environments with competing priorities and differing viewpoints.
Lead discussions where stakeholder opinions may be polarized and drive alignment toward enterprise outcomes.
Negotiate priorities, funding, resource commitments, and roadmap decisions across organizational boundaries.
Influence and build consensus without authority in a highly matrixed global environment.
Present program strategy, risks, decisions, and results to executive and governance forums.
Innovation & Capability Development
Identify new capabilities required to support enterprise data and AI strategies.
Evaluate emerging technologies, tools, and operating practices.
Lead modernization initiatives related to:
Data governance
Metadata platforms
Data quality tooling
Master data platforms
AI-ready data foundations
AI-auditability for data assets

Build communities of practice and increase organizational data management maturity

About The Team

Deloitte Technology works at the forefront of technology development and processes to support and protect Deloitte around the world. In this truly global environment, we operate not in "what is" but rather "what can be" to help Deloitte deliver and connect with its clients, its communities, and one another in ways not previously conceived.

Enough About Us, Let’s Talk About You

Key Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Information Management, Computer Science, Data Management, Business, or related discipline. Master's degree preferred.
12+ years of experience in enterprise data management, data governance, data architecture, or related disciplines.
7+ years leading global teams and enterprise-scale transformation initiatives.
Proven leadership of master data, metadata, data quality, taxonomy, or data governance programs as the voice of the business with technical teams, particularly for cross-domain data assets. Experience with data governance tools such as Informatica, SAP MDG, Collibra, Databricks Unity Catalog, etc.
Experience establishing operating models and governance frameworks across multiple business units and geographies. Experience working closely with application and operations teams in large, federated organizations.
Confident communicator with the ability to engage effectively with executive leadership teams. Able to translate complex data concepts into business outcomes.
Ability to build strong relationships across organizational boundaries, acting as a trusted advisor to executives, business leaders, architects, product teams, and internal customers represented across multiple geographies.
Demonstrated experience navigating politically complex environments and skilled at facilitating alignment where competing objectives exist, to successfully balance enterprise objectives with individual stakeholder requirements.
Connects enterprise data capabilities to business strategy, operational effectiveness, and AI enablement by establishing measurable outcomes and accountability structures.
Drives execution through governance, influence, and disciplined delivery management leading direct reports and dotted line teams.

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $140,000 - $260,000, and individuals may be eligible to participate in our bonus program. Deloitte is fair and competitive when it comes to the salaries of our people. We regularly benchmark across a variety of positions, industries, sectors, targets, and levels. Our approach is grounded on recognizing people's unique strengths and contributions and rewarding the value that they deliver.

Our Total Rewards Package extends well beyond traditional compensation and benefit programs and is designed to recognize employee contributions, encourage personal wellness, and support firm growth. Along with a competitive base salary and variable pay opportunities, we offer a wide array of initiatives that differentiate us as a people-first organization. On top of our regular paid vacation days, some examples include: $4,000 per year for mental health support benefits, a $1,300 flexible benefit spending account, firm-wide closures known as "Deloitte Days", dedicated days of for learning (known as Development and Innovation Days), flexible work arrangements and a hybrid work structure.

Our promise to our people: Deloitte is where potential comes to life.

Be yourself, and more.

We are a group of talented people who want to learn, gain experience, and develop skills. Wherever you are in your career, we want you to advance.

You Shape How We Make Impact.

Diverse perspectives and life experiences make us better. Whoever you are and wherever you’re from, we want you to feel like you belong here. We provide flexible working options to support you and how you can contribute.

Be the leader you want to be

Some guide teams, some change culture, some build essential expertise. We offer opportunities and experiences that support your continuing growth as a leader.

Have as many careers as you want.

We are uniquely able to offer you new challenges and roles – and prepare you for them. We bring together people with unique experiences and talents, and we are the place to develop a lasting network of friends, peers, and mentors.

The next step is yours

jobs.title: Director, Analytics & Insights
jobs.description:
Department:
Technology

Location:
Toronto, ON

Compensation:
CA$130,000 - CA$170,000 / year

Description

What we do every day to be our very best

Every day at Securian Canada means a day spent helping Canadians and their families build secure tomorrows. We’re agile and innovative, and we aren't afraid to challenge and create, or bring diverse perspectives to our work.

Who We Need

As our Director, Analytics & Insights
, you'll help shape how data drives decisions across Securian Canada.

We're looking for a leader who sees beyond dashboards and reports. Someone who is energized by complex business challenges, naturally curious about what drives performance, and passionate about transforming data into meaningful business outcomes. You'll play a pivotal role in building and evolving an enterprise analytics capability
that empowers leaders with trusted insights, scalable analytics products, modern business intelligence, and practical AI-enabled solutions
.

Reporting to the AVP, Data Solutions, you'll lead a multidisciplinary team
responsible for Analytics & Insights, Business Intelligence, and Analytics Engineering. Working across business and technology teams, you'll help create a shared understanding of customers, products, markets, financial performance, and organizational priorities, enabling smarter decisions at every level of the organization.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with hands-on leadership
. You'll influence enterprise priorities
, guide complex analytical initiatives, challenge assumptions, and help leaders translate insights into action.

The leader we're looking for combines strong business judgment with technical depth
. You start with the decision that needs to be made, not the tool that will be used. You understand that data and analytics are strategic business assets
and know how to balance immediate business needs with scalable enterprise solutions. You're pragmatic, collaborative, governance-minded, and skilled at translating complex analytical concepts into compelling business narratives that drive action.

Most importantly, you're passionate about building high-performing teams
, developing talent
, fostering collaboration, and creating an environment where people can do their best work while making a meaningful impact
.

At Securian Canada, analytics is about more than understanding what happened. It's about helping people make better decisions that support our mission of helping Canadians and their families build secure tomorrows. You'll join a team of talented professionals who are committed to innovation, continuous improvement, and creating solutions that make a real difference across our business.

The base salary range for this position is between $130,000 to $170,000 depending on experience. Details of our additional benefits are outlined below. This job posting is for an existing vacancy. Only one position is available. However, it may be based in multiple locations: Toronto (ON), or Waterloo (ON), or Montreal (QC).

What You Will Do

Lead Enterprise Analytics Strategy & Decision Support

Define and execute an analytics and insights roadmap aligned with enterprise, market, customer, and partner priorities.
Transform strategic business questions into actionable analytical opportunities, KPI frameworks, data requirements, and decision-support solutions.
Deliver meaningful insights into business performance, customer behaviour, claims experience, product results, portfolio trends, operational effectiveness, and emerging risks.
Translate complex findings into clear recommendations and executive-ready narratives that drive informed decision-making.
Establish scalable practices that improve prioritization, delivery, adoption, value realization, and continuous improvement.

Build Modern Analytics Products & Business Intelligence Capabilities

Lead the evolution from fragmented reporting toward trusted, enterprise-scale analytics products.
Oversee the development of curated datasets, semantic models, certified metrics, dashboards, scorecards, and client-facing reporting solutions.
Partner with Data Pipeline Engineering, Technology, Governance, Finance, and business leaders to strengthen analytics foundations and support critical business priorities.
Improve self-service analytics capabilities while reducing manual effort, duplicated logic, and disconnected solutions.
Ensure analytics products are scalable, reliable, understandable, and centered around real business decisions.

Advance AI, Machine Learning & Analytical Innovation

Identify practical opportunities where advanced analytics, machine learning, predictive modeling, and AI can create measurable business value.
Prioritize initiatives based on business impact, data readiness, adoption potential, and long-term sustainability.
Establish governance, controls, explainability, data quality standards, and operating requirements needed to support responsible AI and advanced analytics.
Guide innovative solutions from ideation through implementation, ensuring clear ownership, measurable outcomes, and long-term success.

Develop High-Performing Teams & Analytics Capabilities

Lead, coach, and inspire a team of professionals across analytics, insights, business intelligence, reporting, and analytics engineering.
Foster a culture focused on analytical excellence, collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and business partnership.
Provide guidance on analytical problem solving, data-product design, storytelling, and stakeholder engagement.
Help team members grow beyond traditional reporting by strengthening skills in problem framing, root-cause analysis, insight generation, and strategic recommendations.
Create an environment where innovation, curiosity, and measurable business outcomes are valued and celebrated.

Build Strong Partnerships Across the Organization

Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, helping connect business priorities to data-driven solutions.
Build strong relationships across Data Solutions, Technology, Finance, Operations, and business teams.
Influence decision-making by bringing clarity, insight, and strategic perspective to complex challenges.
Champion a data-informed culture that increases confidence, consistency, and trust in organizational decision-making.

What You Will Bring

University degree in Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, Business, or a related quantitative discipline.
10+ years of progressive experience in analytics, business intelligence, analytics engineering, data science, decision support, or related fields, including leadership responsibilities.
Demonstrated success building, transforming, or significantly advancing enterprise analytics capabilities within a complex organization.
Strong experience translating ambiguous business challenges into actionable analytical solutions, meaningful insights, and measurable outcomes.
Deep expertise in SQL, Python, analytical data modeling, business intelligence platforms, and modern cloud data environments.
Experience developing scalable analytical datasets, curated data products, KPI frameworks, semantic models, and enterprise reporting solutions.
Strong understanding of modern data ecosystems, from source systems and data engineering through analytics delivery and business consumption.
Experience applying advanced analytics, machine learning, predictive modeling, or AI-enabled solutions to business challenges.
Proven ability to influence executive stakeholders while effectively leading highly technical teams.
Strong leadership capabilities with experience building, mentoring, and developing high-performing teams.
Experience within insurance, financial services, or another regulated industry is considered an asset.
Experience with cloud data warehouses, lakehouse architectures, and modern self-service BI platforms.
Knowledge of responsible AI practices, model governance, data quality, lineage, explainability, and operational controls.
Exceptional communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to simplify complexity and inspire action through data.
A strategic and product-oriented mindset focused on delivering sustainable, scalable solutions that create long-term business value.

Why join?

When you’re a part of Securian Canada, you’re a member of an agile and innovative, high-performing, bright-thinking, make-things-happen culture – so that together, we can discover the art of possible.

At our company, we see your potential on day one and challenge you to grow your unique strengths as you create a career filled with opportunity, collaboration, and purpose.

You’ll also be part of a team that’s committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and who values diverse perspectives, so that you can be the person you want to be – both in, and outside, work.

Securian Canada offers a competitive total rewards program with a variety of perks and benefits, including:

Flexible work arrangements with monthly financial allocations to support your work-life balance;
Generous starting paid vacation time, plus additional vacation days for every year of service;
Paid volunteer day so you can dedicate time to a cause you are passionate about;
Paid personal and wellness days to support your total wellbeing;
Educational assistance of up to $3,500 a year (with approval from your manager);
Flexible health and wellness account (in addition to comprehensive drug and dental coverage) to help pay for a wide range of wellbeing services that are meaningful to you;
Up to 14% of combined contributions to the RRSP matching program;
Family-friendly maternity/parental leave and,
Many more benefits, perks and programs.

If you have at least 70% of the qualifications we're looking for, want to work in a fast-growing, leading and progressive company, and feel driven to help Canadians and their families build secure futures – we want to hear from you!

Take the first step in building your future with Securian Canada. Apply now.

jobs.title: Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader in AI-integrated Biomedical Devices
jobs.description:
The Faculty of Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Victoria seeks to recruit a world-class junior faculty member for a Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position in AI-integrated Biomedical Sensors, Diagnostics, and/or Medical Imaging. If awarded, this is a tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level, to commence July 1, 2027. This position is for candidates working in alignment with the Federal Strategic Priority of “health and biotechnology.”

The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program is a $120 million investment to help institutions bring more internationally based early career researchers (ECR) to Canada. This program is administered by the Tri-agency Institutional Programs Secretariat (TIPS). The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position is associated with an Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair and is valued at $100,000 per year over six years. A possible extension is available for six additional years at the same yearly amount and will be contingent on confirming that the recruited ECR has progressed in their academic career and demonstrates the research conducted since the recruitment has been transformational, translational and has garnered partners. 

Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders awards are intended for exceptional early career researchers (ECR). Candidates must be within five years (minus eligible delays) of the start date of their first research-related appointment, defined as an appointment where the individual has the autonomy to conduct research independently. All eligible delays in research (e.g., maternity, parental, medical, bereavement) are credited as twice the amount of time taken. Professional leaves (e.g., training, sabbatical, administrative) are not credited as eligible leaves. Only candidates who are internationally based (both working and residing outside of Canada) as of July 28, 2026, are eligible. Applicants must state in their cover letter that they meet the criteria for an ECR and that they were based outside of Canada as of July 28, 2026.

The candidate’s qualifications, experience, overall market demand and rank will determine a final salary offer. Industry experience is an asset. The salary for this position includes a competitive salary range of $120,000 - $150,000. UVic is committed to offering an equitable and competitive salary, inclusive of a generous benefits package, eligible leaves and pension plan.

Requirements

The ideal applicant will have a strong foundation in next-generation devices or imaging methods that take advantage of recent advances in data science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. This faculty member will join a vibrant, growing community of biomedical engineering researchers at the University of Victoria. This role offers the opportunity to move beyond traditional design and directly integrate cutting-edge artificial intelligence algorithms into complex real-world medical practice.
The successful candidate is expected to demonstrate deep expertise in one or more areas related to next-generation devices and approaches, with the expressed goal of improving patient outcomes at scale, improving equity of access to healthcare, and delivering cost savings to the public. Possible application areas include, but are not limited to the following:
AI-based sensors and wearable devices for remote, secure, and respectful monitoring of patient data and health in Indigenous and other underserved communities.
AI- and ML-based methods for image processing and medical imaging via X-ray, MRI, ultrasound, spectroscopy, or other modalities.

The successful applicant will:
be appointed to the Department of Mechanical Engineering and/or Electrical and Computer Engineering at the rank of Assistant Professor;
contribute to the design and delivery of course-based curricula for the Biomedical Engineering students at the undergraduate and graduate levels; and
interact with other relevant members of the scholarly community at UVic, within and outside the Faculty of Engineering and Computer Science.

The successful applicant will:
hold (or be on the verge of completing) a Ph.D. in biomedical engineering or a relevant engineering discipline;
be a registered professional engineer in Canada, or be eligible to apply for registration with the Engineers and Geoscientists of British Columbia (details available at www.egbc.ca);
have clear ideas and aspirations to contribute to the Biomedical Engineering Program’s drive to increase the diversity of our student population and foster a supportive and inclusive environment for all;
possess excellent communication skills with an ability to communicate research vision, methods, rationale and impacts across a diverse array of audiences; and
demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in undergraduate and graduate engineering education as evidenced by:
potential for excellence in teaching courses related to the Biomedical Engineering discipline, and,
an inclusive approach to mentoring and supervising diverse students both in classroom and in research environments.

Please note that the requirement for the candidate to hold or be near completion of a Ph.D. is a requirement of the University of Victoria and not the Impact+ Program.

Additional information
The University acknowledges that career interruptions and slowdowns may affect a candidate’s record of research achievement and, when applicable, encourages applicants to describe these impacts in their application. Life circumstances such as illness, disability, family and community responsibilities (including parental leave, caregiving responsibilities, illness-related leave, chronic illness or disability, and COVID-19-related disruptions) are a normal part of life and may influence a nominee’s research record. These circumstances will be carefully considered during the assessment process. Applications are encouraged from individuals who have experienced career interruptions for parental or other types of leaves (see https://www.canada.ca/en/research-coordinating-committee/priorities/support-early-career-researchers.html for information on how career interruptions affect Early Career Researcher eligibility).

To safeguard research in academia, the Government of Canada has implemented the Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern (STRAC) and the National Security Guidelines for Research Partnerships (NSGRP). These Research Security policies apply to the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program. UVic recommends applicants to review these policies to ensure alignment with Research Security considerations of research funding programs. Vetting of shortlisted candidates will be integrated into the adjudication process for this competition. When awarded the Emerging Leader position, the successful applicant must not have any active affiliation with any entity on Canada’s List of Named Research Organizations (NRO) of concern and must maintain this status throughout their tenure as Emerging Leader.

Faculty and Librarians at the University of Victoria are governed by the provisions of the Collective Agreement. Members are represented by the University of Victoria Faculty Association.

Contact information
Candidates should submit a single PDF document that includes:

a cover letter providing an overview of the candidate’s qualifications and how their research experience would complement the position as described; the cover letter must also state that the applicant meets the criteria for an ECR (i.e. they are within five years of their first research-related appointment, minus eligible delays) and that they were working and residing outside of Canada as of July 28, 2026.
a detailed curriculum vitae;
a max 2-page description of the candidate’s proposed research program;
a max 1-page description of the candidate’s teaching experience and philosophy;
a max 1-page statement on how a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion would be embodied in the teaching and research activities. In forming their EDI statement, applicants are asked to refer to the Equity Action Plan, particularly its 5 universal goals, and elaborate on how they would build and lead a diverse research team that champions inclusivity, ensures that all members have the opportunity to reach their full potential and works to create opportunities for meaningful collaborations across the UVic campus.
contact information for four referees.

To be considered, please submit your application package via email to eceasst@uvic.ca with the subject line “AI-Integrated Devices: Asst Prof. position” by December 4, 2026. Applications should be addressed to: Dr. John White.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Amy Issel, Assistant to the Chair
+1-250-721-8614
eceasst@uvic.ca
Please note that reference and background checks, including credential and degree verification, may be undertaken as part of this recruitment process.

jobs.title: VP, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
About Us

Opensity Solutions is the largest tech‑enabled managed services organization serving leading law firms, financial institutions and professional services firms. At Opensity, we provide integrated operational platforms, automation and advisory services that enable clients to modernize operating models, reduce cost and accelerate growth. Our capabilities include IT and technology solutions, document processing and administrative support, marketing and communications, billing and AP/AR services, records and information governance, workflow automation, consulting and hospitality and facilities services.

Our Mission

Our mission is to provide modernized technology platforms, elevated technology support, and valuable insights, empowering our clients to excel in what they do best.

Who We Are

Opensity Solutions is the largest end-to-end, tech-enabled managed services organization focused on serving leading law firms, financial institutions and professional services firms.

Launched in 2026 through the combination of K2 Services, Epiq GBTS and Forrest Solutions, Opensity brings together more than 4,500 professionals, 500+ clients and over $400 million in combined annual revenue, with operations across the United States, Canada, India and the Philippines.

Our mission is to provide modernized technology platforms, elevated technology support and valuable insights, empowering our clients to excel in what they do best.

Opensity is backed by Renovus Capital Partners, a leading private equity sponsor with deep experience investing in and scaling technology-enabled services businesses.

For more information, visit opensitysolutions.com
.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis
to lead enterprise-wide planning, forecasting, management reporting and business performance analytics. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer
, this role will be a key partner to executive leadership, business unit leaders and our private equity sponsor. The VP, FP&A will help build a scalable, data-driven FP&A function and play an important role in Opensity's continued growth, M&A activity and long-term value creation.

Key Responsibilities

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting and long-range planning across the organization.
Own monthly and quarterly management reporting, variance analysis and executive performance reviews.
Develop actionable financial and operational KPIs across revenue, margin, headcount, productivity, cash flow and profitability.
Build robust recurring revenue analytics, including bookings, backlog, retention, churn, expansion and customer-level performance.
Partner with business leaders to improve forecast accuracy, financial accountability and operating performance.
Lead customer, service-line and business-unit profitability analysis to support pricing, investment and resource allocation decisions.
Drive automation and modernization of FP&A, including dashboards, reporting, forecasting and data analysis.
Support the CFO with Board, lender and private equity sponsor reporting.
Support M&A diligence, integration, synergy tracking and post-acquisition performance management.
Help maintain a strong, diligence-ready Finance organization and support future refinancing, recapitalization or exit processes.
Lead and develop the FP&A team.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field.
10+ years of progressive Finance experience, including significant FP&A leadership experience.
Private equity-backed company experience required.
Experience working through a private equity exit, sale process, recapitalization or similar transaction strongly preferred.
Strong experience with recurring revenue businesses and associated KPIs and analytics.
Meaningful M&A and post-acquisition integration experience required.
Strong data analytics capabilities with demonstrated experience automating financial reporting and analysis.
Experience in technology-enabled services, managed services, professional services, business services or SaaS strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting and executive presentation skills.
Experience working with Boards, senior executives and private equity sponsors.
Experience with planning, ERP and BI tools such as Sage Intacct, Adaptive, Anaplan, OneStream, Power BI or similar platforms.
CPA, CFA or MBA preferred but not required.
Strong leadership, communication and business-partnering skills.

What We Offer

Competitive compensation and performance-based annual bonus.
Comprehensive health and wellness benefits.
Remote-first flexibility.
Significant exposure to executive leadership, the Board and private equity sponsor.
Meaningful involvement in M&A, integrations and strategic value-creation initiatives.
The opportunity to help build the Finance function of a large, newly formed and growing organization.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
CarltonOne is a global B2B technology leader, and part of the Goldman Sachs portfolio, helping organizations around the world reward and inspire exceptional people. Our solutions empower employees to be more productive, sales teams to perform at their best, and customers to stay engaged and loyal.

Our platform powers the global engagement industry, enabling companies to deliver impactful employee recognition, customer loyalty, rewards, sales, and channel incentive programs. We partner with over 450 clients
, 500 vendors
, and serve 14 million members
across 185 countries
.

Beyond engagement, every CarltonOne solution drives our eco-action mission: funding tree planting to help restore the planet. To date, we’ve funded over 21 million trees
and are on track to plant millions more each year. Learn more at carltonone.com .

About the Opportunity:

CarltonOne is seeking a highly motivated Director, Information Technology to lead CarltonOne's global enterprise IT function, owning IT strategy, service management, governance, and employee technology experience.

This role is responsible for delivering a best-in-class employee technology experience across the organization, ensuring employees have the tools, systems, support, and infrastructure they need to be productive and successful. The Director, IT will lead internal IT support, service delivery, endpoint management, identity and access management, collaboration tools, workplace technology initiatives, and global hardware operations across CarltonOne's international workforce.

This is a strategic leadership role. The Director, IT is accountable for the outcomes of IT service delivery rather than working the support queue, leading through managers, team leads, and managed service partners who handle Level 1 and Level 2 support. The Director serves as the senior escalation point and leader during major IT and security incidents, and focuses on strengthening process, governance, and measurement to deliver an exceptional, proactive employee experience. The successful candidate will focus on improving service levels, modernizing IT processes, strengthening security practices, and scaling internal technology operations to support a growing global organization.

Responsibilities:

IT Service Management & Incident Leadership

Own CarltonOne's global IT operating model, including service desk structure, tiered support (L1/L2/L3), escalation paths, and the balance of in-house and managed service provider (MSP) coverage.
Hold the service desk and support partners accountable for timely, high-quality resolution of employee requests and issues, without personally working day-to-day L1/L2 tickets.
Define and publish SLAs, experience level agreements (XLAs), and an IT performance scorecard covering CSAT, first-contact resolution, mean time to resolve, SLA attainment, backlog age, and reopen rates, reported monthly to executive leadership.

Ensure consistent delivery of IT services across all regions and time zones.
Act as Major Incident Manager and senior escalation point for high-impact IT outages, leading coordinated response, stakeholder communications, and service restoration.

Implement a problem management practice that uses root cause analysis and post-incident reviews to eliminate recurring issues, with tracked corrective actions.
Establish change, release, and configuration management processes that reduce change-related incidents and protect service stability.
Own Jira Service Management as the IT service management platform, driving workflow design, automation, SLA tracking, and reporting.
Partner with SaaS production, engineering, and DevOps teams to align IT processes such as access, change, and incident management with production operations, and provide the internal tools and access they need.

Shift IT from reactive to proactive by using monitoring, digital employee experience (DEX) tooling, and endpoint analytics to detect and resolve issues before employees are affected.
Measure employee technology sentiment through regular surveys and an IT Net Promoter Score, and act on the results with visible follow-through.
Promote a shift-left approach that moves common requests to self-service and automation, freeing the team for higher-value work.
Create seamless onboarding and offboarding experiences through standardized technology processes.

Own CarltonOne's global hardware procurement, deployment, lifecycle management, and asset governance strategy.

Partner with global vendors, distributors, and logistics providers to ensure timely delivery, replacement, retrieval, and support of employee equipment worldwide.
Establish global standards for laptops, peripherals, mobile devices, and collaboration technology to provide a consistent employee experience.

Establish reporting and KPIs related to deployment timelines, inventory accuracy, hardware utilization, asset recovery, and employee satisfaction.

Promote knowledge sharing, process consistency, and operational excellence across the team.
Build a high-performing IT organization capable of supporting a rapidly growing global workforce.

Ensure reliable operation of corporate productivity platforms including Microsoft 365, communication platforms, and workplace technologies.
Support office technology infrastructure across multiple global locations.
Own software licensing and SaaS governance, including licence optimization, application rationalization, and shadow IT controls.
Identify opportunities to modernize and standardize workplace technology solutions.

Identity, Access Management & IT Security

jobs.title: Director of Finance and Administration
jobs.description:
Lead financial and corporate stewardship for Curve Lake First Nation

Step into a senior leadership role offering a competitive $150,000 to $180,000 annual salary, negotiable based on qualifications, plus excellent benefits!

Build the systems, teams, and financial stability that will support the Nation for the next decade

About Curve Lake First Nation

Curve Lake First Nation is an Anishinaabe community with deep roots in this territory, grounded in relationships to land, water, and each other as Curve Lakers. Known historically as Mud Lake, Curve Lake continues as a living, resilient Nation of almost 3,000 members. As part of the Michi Saagiig Anishinaabeg and signatories to the Williams Treaties, the community carries forward its responsibilities, teachings, and governance systems. Curve Lake is a place of strong kinship, cultural continuity, and collective responsibility, where each member contributes to the wellbeing of the Nation. Our community is located just north of the City of Peterborough, Ontario.

Home to trailblazers like Elsie Knott, Canada's first Anishinaabe Kwe O'gimaa, and renowned artisans, our community blends rich history with vibrant culture. More than an employer, we're a community of choice. Join us in preserving traditions, fostering diversity, and contributing to a future where old ways merge seamlessly with progress. Shape the legacy of Curve Lake—a place where heritage meets opportunity.

To learn more about us, please visit: curvelakefirstnation.ca

About the Opportunity

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Finance and Administration
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.
This role joins the organization during a period of organizational transition and growth.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will provide strategic leadership across the Nation’s corporate functions. These are financial governance, human resources, policy and planning, communications, and information technology. Finance sits at the heart of the role. You will be accountable for sound financial oversight, audit readiness, and strong relationships with funders, auditors, and the First Nations Financial Management Board.

Where We Are Now

The Nation is strengthening its administrative foundations; you will provide interim oversight and stabilization across Finance, HR, IT, and Policy and Planning while building out your team. You will also lead the selection and implementation of a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.

A key priority is moving the Nation from year-by-year funding to Indigenous Services Canada’s 10-year grant. This means completing the Financial Management Board certification process and putting the controls and reporting in place to qualify. Predictable, long-term funding will give the Nation far greater confidence in its forecasting and planning.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, success will mean a fully staffed division with your managers in place, trusted relationships with Chief and Council, staff, and community, strengthened audit readiness and internal controls, and the ERP selection well underway.

By the end of year two, you will have led the Nation through FMB certification and embedded consistent financial, governance, and administrative practices. You will also have put systems in place that keep reporting and audits on schedule, giving the organization a solid foundation for the years ahead.

Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Leading multi-year financial planning, forecasting, and annual operating and capital budgets
Serving as executive lead for external audits, including selecting the appropriate audit firm and working closely with auditors throughout the process
Ensuring compliance with funding agreements, Indigenous Services Canada reporting requirements, and the Nation’s Financial Administration Law
Leading the Nation through the FMB certification and 10-year grant process
Structuring and staffing the finance function so reporting deadlines are consistently met, working with bookkeepers, analysts, and account managers
Providing executive oversight of HR, IT, policy and planning, and communications through four direct-report managers
Overseeing the selection and implementation of an ERP system, along with cybersecurity, data governance, and digital modernization
Providing financial analysis, risk advice, and recommendations to the Executive Director and Chief and Council

Due to the role's significance, refer to the Director of Finance and Administration document for a comprehensive overview beyond the listed duties.

More About You

To qualify, you will need a post-secondary degree or diploma in finance, accounting, or a related financial field
, along with at least 5 years of senior-level experience in financial administration or corporate services,
including experience working within a First Nation organization.

The following are required:
A valid Class G Driver’s Licence
Ability to undergo a criminal background check and vulnerable sector check
Willingness and ability to travel as required

The following skills and experience will be strong assets:
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation
Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM) or Certified Aboriginal Professional Administrator (CAPA) designation
A master’s degree in public administration, finance, or a related field
Direct experience with the First Nations Financial Management Board, FMB certification, or the 10-year grant process
Strong working knowledge of audit processes, GAAP, and funder reporting requirements
Experience working with Indigenous Services Canada and other funding agencies
Experience overseeing multiple functional areas such as Finance, HR, IT, and Planning

As our ideal candidate, you are a disciplined, systems-minded leader who keeps deadlines met and audits clean, and who knows how to build a finance team organized around its reporting obligations. Your understanding of First Nation finances runs from day-to-day funding agreements through to the path toward long-term grant funding. Just as importantly, you lead with integrity, calm, and a people-centred approach, bringing an awareness of intergenerational trauma and its impact on workplaces and governance, along with a genuine respect for Curve Lake First Nation’s history, culture, and traditions.

Note: Preference will be given to applicants who have First Nation or Indigenous ancestry.

About the Benefits

In exchange for your hard work and dedication, you will receive a highly competitive salary of $150,000 to $180,000
negotiable dependent on experience, along with a great host of benefits, including:
Relocation assistance
Comprehensive Benefits Plan: extended health care, dental, vision, life and long-term disability, etc.
Competitive Pension Plan with up to 7.5% employer matching
40 paid hours for Special/Personal Leave Bereavement Leave
Paid time off for 17 designated days, including National Indigenous Day, Christmas Day, etc.
Generous vacation accrual
Paid sick days
Regular community events such as Pow Wows, Harvesters' Gatherings, Christmas Craft Shows, and more!

Take on a senior leadership role that builds lasting financial stability and strong systems for the Curve Lake First Nation community. Apply now!

jobs.description:
Be part of the journey!

Our mission is to be the preferred airline of our customers and our team.

Open-mindedness, concern for others, intelligence at work and, above all, a healthy dose of fun enable us to achieve great things every day. Our dedication has earned us the title of the world's best leisure airline multiple times, and we’re just getting started.

Want to join us? You will have the chance to enjoy exclusive travel privileges to explore the world and create unforgettable memories. You will also have the opportunity to work in a modern, inspiring environment.

Job Description

Reporting to the Senior Director, Finance, the Director – Financial Reporting and Optimization acts as a key strategic partner within Air Transat’s finance function.

A true change agent and mobilizing leader, the incumbent drives the evolution and continuous improvement of financial processes to support the organization’s growth and performance.

As a trusted business partner, they work closely with multidisciplinary teams, as well as financial and operational leaders, to transform financial data into high-value insights that support decision-making.

Responsibilities

Provide leadership, guidance, and development to a team of financial analysts, fostering a collaborative, rigorous, and high-performance environment
Ensure the proper execution of accounting activities and maintain strong internal controls related to Air Transat’s airline costs and balance sheet
Coordinate and review accounting provisions related to aircraft leases and aeronautical components in compliance with IFRS 16
Oversee the consolidation of the Company’s financial results, for both statutory and management reporting purposes, and ensure data accuracy and reliability
Lead the budgeting process, financial planning, and in-depth analysis of areas under their responsibility (maintenance, capital expenditures, IFRS 16)
Oversee the preparation and review of Air Transat’s statutory financial statements, ensuring accuracy and compliance
Ensure the ongoing application of IFRS standards for complex transactions, particularly related to maintenance, and lead the implementation of new accounting standards
Play a key role in implementing innovative solutions and continuous improvement initiatives within the finance function
Build and maintain strong business relationships with leaders and act as a trusted strategic advisor
Lead special finance-related projects and actively contribute to strategic decision-making

Qualifications

Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation – required
Minimum of 7 years of experience in personnel management within a financial environment
Experience in a large organization; experience in the aviation industry is considered a strong asset
In-depth knowledge of IFRS standards and their practical application
Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite tools
Proven leadership and strong ability to influence diverse stakeholders
Demonstrated experience in change management and organizational transformation
Strong ability to analyze complex situations and make sound decisions quickly
Oral and written fluency in French and English *

*A good knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec. The incumbent will be required to communicate and collaborate frequently in English, both orally and in writing, with colleagues, customers, and other stakeholders in Quebec, the rest of Canada, and internationally.

Additional Information

Artificial intelligence tools are used to analyze applications, whether to sort or preselect profiles based on criteria related to job requirements. All applications are then reviewed by our recruitment team to ensure a fair and inclusive process.

Employment Equity

At Transat, we foster an environment where inclusiveness, respect and equity reign. We endeavour to build a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers as well as the communities to which we travel. We encourage women, members of visible minorities, ethnic minorities, aboriginal peoples as well as people with disabilities to submit their candidacy. Transat will accommodate people with disabilities throughout the recruitment and selection process. If you require an accommodation, please contact us in order to work together in meeting adequately your needs.
